mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered agent, company secretary, or corporate UBO itself

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter for the founding shareholder(s)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and senior officers against the UN Consolidated Sanctions List, UK OFSI Consolidated List, UK Sanctions and Anti-Money Laundering Act 2018 designations, EU consolidated financial sanctions, and US OFAC SDN and Non-SDN Consolidated Lists; enhanced due diligence (EDD) applied to all PEPs and family/close associates; adverse media and negative news checks required; ongoing transaction monitoring under CIMA AML/CFT Rules and FATF Recommendation 12; all results documented in the client risk assessment file.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Cayman Islands General Registry (CIGR) eServices Portal — https://eservices.cigr.gov.ky
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All proposed names must use the 26-letter modern English (Roman/Latin) alphabet only; diacritical marks, characters of non-Latin scripts, and transliterations into non-Roman scripts are not accepted. The name must end with an approved legal form element such as 'Limited', 'Ltd', 'Corporation', 'Inc', or an abbreviation acceptable to the Registrar, and must not misrepresent the company's legal status, business scope, or relationship with any government or Crown entity.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the licensed corporate service provider (CSP) may file a written administrative appeal with the Registrar of Companies within 21 calendar days of the rejection notice, attaching concise legal submissions addressing the stated grounds for refusal; alternatively, the CSP may immediately submit a fresh reservation with an amended name. Name reservations are not automatically extendable; after expiry of the 90-day reservation window, a new reservation application and applicable fee must be submitted to the CIGR eServices portal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A physical registered office within the Cayman Islands is statutorily mandatory and must be maintained at all times by a licensed corporate service provider; the no-code website builder's operational activities, software development, and digital sales may be conducted entirely remotely without physical Caymanian presence, but the registered office functions as the legal service-of-process and statutory correspondence address. Pure virtual-office arrangements lacking a physical Cayman address or licensed resident agent capacity are not permissible.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified as approximately 5–10% annual probability for a standard low-risk entity; CIMA and the General Registry retain unrestricted statutory powers of unannounced physical inspection under the Monetary Authority Act (2021 Revision) and the Companies Act (2021 Revision), and the probability increases materially upon any regulatory complaint, suspicious transaction report, or PEP-linked UBO.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Cayman Islands Companies Act (2024 Revision), ss. 4-13 (formation), s. 24 (registered office), ss. 179-183 (exempted companies); UK overseas company registration under Part 34, Companies Act 2006 and the Overseas Companies Regulations 2009 (SI 2009/1801)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cayman Islands General Registry, Registrar of Companies (incorporation); UK Companies House, Register of Overseas Companies (UK establishment registration)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association filed under s. 13(1) of the Companies Act; Certificate of Incorporation; UK Form OS IN01 filed under the Overseas Companies Regulations 2009, reg. 5
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; no escrow account requirement; no capital duty. Standard exempted company adopts authorised share capital of US$50,000 (incorporation fee US$1,190); annual government fee of US$1,190 applies for authorised capital up to US$50,000.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscribers adopt the Memorandum and Articles of Association as filed, and that the registered office at [Provider Address], Grand Cayman, be confirmed, with [Provider] appointed as registered office and corporate secretary. RESOLVED, that the directors named in the Register of Directors are appointed, with [Name] as Chief Executive Officer and [Name] as Chief Financial Officer, each authorized to open and operate bank and payment accounts, execute commercial agreements, and register the Company as an overseas company in the United Kingdom. RESOLVED, that any director is authorized to file statutory returns, pay formation and government fees, and engage professional advisers as required for the Company's no-code web platform business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name reservation and clearance for exempted-company registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cayman Islands General Registry - Corporate Affairs, Registrar of Companies (Name Reservation Desk)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit 2-3 proposed names ending in Limited or Ltd. via the engaged Cayman-licensed corporate service provider. The Registrar checks the proposed names against the register and prohibited terms, and issues a name-reservation direction valid for 90 days. The application may be delivered electronically; no name publication is required for exempted companies.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and two alternatives
Certificate of Identity of the first subscriber
Declaration of principal business (no-code software)
Registered-office provider engagement letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for identity or similarity, file a written rebuttal with trade-mark and goodwill evidence within 30 days, or reserve an alternative name. Re-submission requires no additional government fee if made within the 90-day reservation window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and execution of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The provider drafts the M&A in English, including the objects clause, authorised share capital of US$50,000 divided into ordinary shares, and standard exempted-company declarations. The first subscriber executes the M&A; execution may be effected electronically or by wet-ink signature witnessed by a notary. Notarised and apostilled copies are retained for the subsequent UK registration and payment-processor due diligence.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association (English)
Subscriber appointment and share allocation schedule
Passport copies of subscriber and proposed directors
Director consent forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the provider identifies drafting conflicts or omitted regulated activities, amend the M&A before filing; no Registrar penalty arises because the document is pre-clearance. For activities requiring consent, add a special resolution of consent prior to filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of M&A and issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cayman Islands General Registry, Registrar of Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed M&A together with the statement of nominal share capital with the Registrar under s. 13(1) of the Companies Act. Pay the official government fee of US$1,190 for authorised capital up to US$50,000. The Registrar verifies compliance and issues the Certificate of Incorporation, which evidences separate legal personality and limited liability from the date of issue.
required_dossiers: Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association (original)
Statement of nominal share capital
Government fee payment receipt
Name reservation certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries the objects or share-capital statement, submit a corrected statement within 14 days; correction fees are nominal and no penalty accrues provided the company does not transact before the Certificate is issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation statutory registers and appointment of officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cayman Islands General Registry (register inspection) / registered-office provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the statutory books at the registered office: Register of Members, Register of Directors, and Register of Charges. Enter the initial share allotment and director appointments, appoint the corporate secretary, and confirm the registered office under s. 24 of the Companies Act. Issue share certificates to the subscriber and prepare the annual-return declaration for future filing.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Register of Members and share certificates
Register of Directors (names, addresses, passport copies)
Registered office consent and secretary appointment letters
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late or incomplete registers attract a potential default fine; the remedy is immediate replenishment of the register with a covering declaration. Any fine is waivable by the Registrar on good cause shown within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: UK overseas-company registration at Companies House
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: UK Companies House (online OS filing service)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of opening a UK place of business, file Form OS IN01 with certified copies of the Cayman Certificate of Incorporation and M&A, particulars of directors and secretary, UK registered-office address, and persons authorised to accept service. Companies House will issue a UK establishment number in the format BR/UKXXXX. The UK establishment is thereafter subject to annual accounts and confirmation-statement filing obligations.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of Cayman Certificate of Incorporation (apostilled)
Certified English translation of M&A
Form OS IN01 (registration particulars)
Form OS OS01 (appointment of persons authorised to accept service)
Proof of UK registered-office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Companies House rejects the application for defective certification or translation, file amended documents within 14 days of the notice. For late filing, request discretionary acceptance with a written justification letter to avoid penalty proceedings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: HMRC, ICO and commercial registration for UK operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: HMRC (Corporation Tax and VAT), Information Commissioner's Office (ICO), and selected payment providers (Stripe Billing, Paddle)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the overseas company with HMRC for UK tax obligations arising from the UK establishment, maintain evidence of the company's non-UK tax status, and register with the ICO as a data controller with payment of the applicable annual data-protection fee. Complete merchant onboarding with Stripe Billing and Paddle under a low-risk SaaS profile, providing the Cayman certificate and UK Companies House registration extract.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (Cayman)
Companies House UK establishment registration certificate
Director identification and certificate of good standing
Data protection policy and lawful-basis register
Merchant onboarding information for Stripe and Paddle
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If HMRC or ICO raise queries, provide certified translations and a letter of explanation. Any penalty for late ICO registration can be mitigated by voluntary disclosure made before a compliance notice is issued.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Department for Business and Trade (Office for Product Safety and Standards) - not applicable to pure software; Health and Safety Executive (HSE) for UK physical workplace clearance
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - no industrial operating or manufacturing licence required for low-code web application development (ISIC 6201 / NAICS 511210); statutory clearance comprises Companies House registration, ICO data protection registration, and HMRC tax registrations

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment Agency (England), Natural Resources Wales, Scottish Environment Protection Agency (SEPA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - pure software publishing with no manufacturing facilities; no EIA screening or development consent order required under the Town and Country Planning (Environmental Impact Assessment) Regulations 2017
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero industrial discharge; no VOC or waste-water generating processes. Leased office premises comply with WEEE Regulations 2013 for staff computing equipment and UK REACH obligations (not applicable to pure SaaS delivery); cloud data-centre emissions remain outside the company's operational control.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: annual fire-risk assessment and emergency plan under the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005; structural and electrical installation certificates (PAT testing) for any UK office; HSE display-screen-equipment and workplace risk assessments under the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974; building-control completion certificate for any new leasehold fit-out.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Cayman Islands Tax Information Authority (TIA) for local compliance and HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) for UK tax obligations
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Cayman Exempted Companies are exempt from Cayman corporate income tax and do not require a local TIN; foreign entities with UK nexus must register with Companies House for a UK company number and with HMRC for Corporation Tax if carrying on a trade in the UK through a permanent establishment, and for VAT if taxable turnover exceeds the registration threshold
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections available under Cayman law; UK tax treaty provisions may address hybrid mismatches but are not directly applicable without UK tax residency

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: £90,000 annual taxable turnover threshold for mandatory VAT registration in the United Kingdom
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: UK VAT-registered businesses must comply with Making Tax Digital for quarterly VAT returns; real-time VAT reporting becomes mandatory for businesses above specified thresholds from April 2026; e-invoicing standards apply for compliance and may become mandatory for larger entities

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from the UK or services supplied to non-UK customers where the service is performed outside the UK qualify for zero-rating under UK VAT rules; Cayman Exempted Companies without a UK establishment are generally outside the scope of UK VAT
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent or abusive zero-rating claims require full documentation; non-compliance can result in penalties up to 100% of the VAT reclaimed, interest charges, and potential criminal prosecution

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of England (monetary authority and wholesale payments oversight) acting jointly with HM Treasury; outward financial sanctions administration is vested in the Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation (OFSI). The United Kingdom does not maintain a dedicated Foreign Exchange Administration or exchange control authority, and no separate central-bank permit is required for cross-border payments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The United Kingdom maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility of the pound sterling under the largely repealed Exchange Control Act 1947 and the Bank of England's post-1979 liberalisation policy. The Cayman Islands likewise imposes no exchange controls. A Cayman Exempted Company that trades via a UK website builder is therefore free to receive USD/EUR/GBP settlement, convert funds without prior approval, and remit profits abroad. The only practical convertibility hurdle is banking-side de-risking, not state controls. Inward foreign direct investment and outward merchant payments require no BOE consent, provided the counterparty is not subject to OFSI sanctions. If the base operation creates a UK permanent establishment, undistributed profits remain freely convertible, although UK corporate tax returns must disclose remittances and transfer-pricing policies.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory UK or Cayman requirement to surrender export receipts, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no prescribed repatriation timeline for software-as-a-service export proceeds. A Cayman Exempted Company may hold foreign currency in multi-currency settlement accounts indefinitely and convert at commercial rates. However, UK AML and sanctions obligations require that all inward proceeds from Stripe, Paddle, or similar payment facilitators be traceable to end-customer invoices; OFSI reporting applies only where a blocked party or frozen asset is identified.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Treasury Account (GBP) with Multi-Currency Foreign Currency Add-on and Capital Escrow Sub-Account
Business Current Account plus Foreign Currency Account and Available FX Forward Facility
Reserve Accounting and Settlement Concentration Account with Sweep Capability
Cross-Border Multi-Currency Clearing Account focused on Asia-Pacific/USD Corridors
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account; segregated escrow for shareholder funds

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-to-Low with a narrow viable set. Tier-1 UK digital EMIs such as Wise Business, Revolut Business, Tide, and Monese routinely decline Cayman-incorporated applicants under de-risking policies because the Cayman Islands carries an offshore financial centre risk flag. Specialist cross-border EMIs and B2B payment platforms including Airwallex, Currencycloud (Visa Cross-Border Solutions), and subsidiary EEA-passported EMIs may onboard a Cayman Exempted Company only on presentation of the standard offshore documentary package plus economic substance evidence and a UK-regulated introducer. Such EMIs are not licensed to provide traditional overdraft or lending, and they impose daily aggregate clearing caps; they are nevertheless acceptable as complementary settlement rails for Stripe/Paddle payouts. Legal constraint: UK EMIs must operate under the Payment Services Regulations 2017 and the Electronic Money Regulations 2011; a non-EEA Cayman entity may be their customer but may not itself hold an EMI authorisation without a UK establishment.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: UK regulation permits fully remote onboarding under the Money Laundering Regulations 2017 using electronic identity verification, and the Economic Crime and Corporate Transparency Act 2023 supports digital ID checks for directors. In practice, however, tier-1 UK banks treat a Cayman Exempted Company as a higher-risk legal person and typically require one in-person director interview at a UK branch or at the bank's international corporate centre, together with a physical correspondence address in the UK and a written confirmation of the company's place of effective management. Remote opening is achievable only where the applicant holds a pre-existing private banking relationship or is introduced by a UK-regulated accounting or law firm that accepts ongoing compliance responsibility.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore jurisdiction classification of the Cayman Islands as a FATF and EU-monitored financial centre with historical inclusion on non-cooperative list watchlists
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide Cayman Registered Agent Certificate, Certificate of Incorporation, Certificate of Good Standing, updated Register of Directors and beneficial ownership register (economic substance declaration or letter confirming exemption under the International Tax Co-operation (Economic Substance) Law), and a professional reference from a UK-regulated solicitor or chartered accountant confirming the commercial legitimacy of the digital business.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity risk arising from nominee shareholders or a layered ownership chain typical of exempted companies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit verified e-passport copies, proof of residential address to 3 months, signed source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declarations, a complete beneficial ownership chain with percentage holdings, and the Cayman registered office consent letter; all individual directors and ultimate beneficial owners must clear OFSI, UN, and EU sanctions screening before the application is filed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual transaction profile for a no-code website builder: high-volume, low-ticket cross-border subscription revenue with no established UK banking history
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver the Stripe and Paddle settlement reports for the preceding 12 months, CRM billing records, public website URL and domain ownership proof, hosting and infrastructure invoices, privacy policy, End-User Licence Agreement, and board minutes authorising the UK treasury account and appointing authorised signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Single-inflow concentration via third-party payment facilitators creating a clearing-house red flag under UK AML supervisory guidance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide executed merchant services agreements directly with Stripe and Paddle, an IP ownership register evidencing ownership of the visual-template source code, a technical software repository access report, and a written treasury mandate confirming that the UK bank account is the sole concentration account; commit to monthly account officer reviews and an ongoing transaction monitoring procedure.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity and shareholder loan injections from the Cayman treasury or the beneficial owners are routed via SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfer in GBP or USD to the London concentration account. Field 70 purpose-of-payment text must state 'Equity injection for software development entity ISIC 6201' or 'Intercompany working capital loan - no UK tax evasion purpose'. The remitting bank must attach a board resolution of the Cayman company authorising the capital call, a certified source-of-funds letter signed by the ultimate beneficial owners, and the recipient bank's AML form confirming non-sanctioned status. No exchange-control clearance is required, but the receiving bank may complete a purpose-of-payment code under the Bank of England's statistical reporting rules for foreign liabilities; the correct classification for a foreign direct investment equity inflow is to be confirmed by the relationship manager. Incoming settlement from Stripe and Paddle arrives via their acquiring banks as separate daily sweeps using corporate payout MT103s; the UK account name must exactly match the legal name of the Cayman merchant.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for software licensing, cloud infrastructure, subcontractor fees, and vendor settlements utilise four clearing layers: (i) SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfer for foreign-currency payments to non-UK counterparties; (ii) CHAPS for urgent high-value sterling payments within the UK plus SWIFT for correspondent transit; (iii) Faster Payments (FPS) via ISO 20022 PACS.008 for sub-1-million-pound recurring vendor payments inside the UK; and (iv) commercial letters of credit in documentary credit form for material licence acquisitions, typically an irrevocable unconfirmed LC payable by deferred payment at 60 days, advised through a UK clearing bank. Because the United Kingdom has no exchange-control surrender requirement, outbound payments require no dealing licence, but the payee must pass OFSI, UN, and EU consolidated sanctions screening and the board must evidence commercial substance through purchase orders and service contracts.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forward (plain-vanilla GBP/USD and GBP/EUR, contractually traded under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or short-form forex master agreement)
Short-Dated Swap / Roll-Over Forward (previously marketed by UK banks as 'SMF - short maturity forwards')
Zero-Cost FX Collar combining a purchased GBP/USD call option and sold put option with net zero premium at inception
Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swap (GBP/USD) under ISDA 2002 with Credit Support Annex, permissible where the underlying obligation is a commercial borrowing or trade liability
Exchange-Traded FX Futures and options on GBP/USD cleared via ICE Futures Europe or CME, permitted for the corporate treasury of a non-resident Cayman entity without UK bank dealing permission

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return with Annual Government Fee Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cayman Islands Registrar of Companies, General Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 January each calendar year; newly incorporated exempted companies file first annual return in January of the year following incorporation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee accrues under the Cayman Companies Act; if the annual return and government fee remain unpaid, the Registrar may issue a notice of proposed strike-off, dissolve the company, and vest its assets in the Crown.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cayman Islands Department for International Tax Cooperation (DITC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months immediately following the end of the financial year; for a calendar-year exempted company, no later than 31 December of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalties under the International Tax Co-operation (Economic Substance) Act, including a maximum fine of CI$10,000 and daily default penalties of CI$2,000 for continued non-compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Cayman exempted company is not automatically required to obtain an independent audit unless it is a regulated mutual fund, a CIMA licensee (bank, trust, or insurance entity), or expressly required by its articles of association. Non-regulated no-code software builders do not normally meet any audit threshold based solely on turnover or balance sheet size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Cayman Companies Act does not prescribe a distinct statutory accounting framework for exempted companies; financial statements, where prepared, should be prepared in accordance with IFRS as issued by the IASB, with US GAAP acceptable for regulated CIMA licensees when the parent uses US GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Cayman Beneficial Ownership Act, the exempted company must keep an accurate beneficial ownership register at its registered office. The annual return process requires confirmation that the register remains accurate; any changes in beneficial ownership are separately updated in the register and reported to the Registrar within 14 days of the change.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 – USD 20,000 per year when required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (main rate for profits above £250,000; 19% small profits rate for profits below £50,000)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small profits rate of 19% for profits up to £50,000; marginal relief between £50,000 and £250,000; R&D tax relief (up to 33% for SMEs); Patent Box regime (10% effective rate on qualifying IP income); indefinite carryforward of trading losses (subject to 50% restriction on use of carried-forward losses above £5 million).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: CT600 Corporation Tax Return; filed electronically via HMRC's Corporation Tax Online Service or commercial software (e.g., Xero, Sage).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: CT600 must be filed within 12 months after the end of the accounting period; corporation tax payment is due 9 months and 1 day after the end of the accounting period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the legal name as registered with Companies House and the unique taxpayer reference (UTR) issued by HMRC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting period start and end dates
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Specify the period covered by the return, typically 12 months; for a non-resident company, align with the UK tax year if applicable.
Report the accounting profit as per UK GAAP or IFRS, adjusted for tax purposes; non-residents must include UK-source income only.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add back disallowable expenses (e.g., depreciation, client entertainment)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back any expenses not deductible for tax purposes; for non-residents, ensure only UK-related expenses are considered.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduct capital allowances and other reliefs
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim capital allowances on qualifying UK assets; non-residents may claim if the assets are used for UK trade.
Calculate the net taxable profit after adjustments; non-residents must compute UK-source profits only.
Apply the appropriate rate (19% or 25%) to taxable profit; non-residents are subject to the same rates on UK-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits and reliefs (e.g., R&D, Patent Box)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim any applicable reliefs; non-residents must meet specific conditions for UK reliefs.
Net tax due after credits; non-residents must pay via UK bank account or approved payment method.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties: £100 for up to 3 months late; £200 for 3-6 months; £500 for 6-12 months; £1,000 for over 12 months. Additional daily penalties of £10 per day for up to 90 days for returns over 3 months late. Interest on unpaid tax at Bank of England base rate plus 2.5%.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% (UK does not impose withholding tax on dividends paid by UK-resident companies to any shareholder, regardless of residence)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Not applicable for dividends as no WHT is levied. For other income (e.g., royalties, interest), to claim treaty relief, submit Form DT-Individual/Company to HMRC, provide a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the foreign tax authority, and ensure the beneficial ownership test is met. HMRC may require a formal claim within the tax return or via a separate application.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory rate 20%; treaty rate often 0% (e.g., under UK-US, UK-Cayman no treaty, but Cayman has no WHT on outbound royalties). Interest: statutory rate 20%; treaty rate often 0% (e.g., under UK-EU treaties). For Cayman, no treaty exists, so statutory 20% applies unless domestic exemption applies.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File required if related party transactions exceed £1 million (or £5 million for intra-group services); Master File required if group turnover exceeds £50 million and related party transactions exceed £5 million. UK TP rules apply to transactions with related parties, including non-residents.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Cayman Exempted Company is subject to Cayman's Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) if it is tax resident in Cayman. However, if the company is managed and controlled in the UK and thus UK tax resident, it may be exempt from Cayman ESR by filing a tax residency certificate with the Cayman authorities. UK has its own economic substance requirements for certain activities (e.g., IP holding, financing), but for a low-code website builder, the main substance test is having adequate staff, premises, and decision-making in the UK.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating UK taxable profits, failing to register for corporation tax, or concealing UK-source income from HMRC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalties up to 100% of tax understated; criminal prosecution leading to unlimited fines and imprisonment up to 7 years under the Fraud Act 2006 and Finance Act 2007.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally liable for penalties if they knowingly participate in evasion; HMRC may issue personal liability notices, impose travel bans, and seek civil recovery of unpaid tax plus interest.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a Cayman Exempted Company with no real presence in the UK, no employees, no physical office, and no substantive business activities, while claiming UK tax residency or using the Cayman structure to avoid UK tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under UK GAAR (General Anti-Abuse Rule), HMRC can counteract tax advantages, impose penalties up to 60% of the tax counteracted, and deny treaty benefits. Cayman ESR penalties include fines up to KYD 10,000 and imprisonment for directors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for penalties if they fail to ensure the company meets economic substance requirements; HMRC can issue personal liability orders and restrict travel.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to register with HMRC for AML supervision, not conducting customer due diligence (CDD) for clients using the no-code website builder, or processing payments through Stripe/Paddle without proper AML controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to £5,000 per breach, unlimited fines for serious breaches, and imprisonment up to 2 years under the Money Laundering Regulations 2017. HMRC can also suspend or cancel the business's AML registration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally liable for AML failures if they consent or connive; they may face criminal prosecution, civil penalties, and disqualification as directors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to maintain adequate transfer pricing documentation for related party transactions (e.g., charging low fees to a Cayman affiliate for IP or services), or not applying arm's length principles.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: HMRC can adjust profits, impose penalties up to 100% of the additional tax due, and charge interest. For large companies, penalties for non-compliance with documentation can be up to £3,000 per failure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for penalties if they knowingly sign inaccurate returns; HMRC can pursue directors for unpaid tax in cases of deliberate non-compliance.
